issues.title: Ideal-flow flux written as an exact differential

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A_j  := \int_{\partial D_j}  \partial_\nu u (z) \, |dz|= \int_{\partial D_j} \partial_\sigma v(z) \, |dz|, \qquad j \in [M].
If $A_j >0$, we interpret $D_j$ to be a source of the fluid and if $A_j<0$, we interpret $D_j$ to be a sink.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the flux across \partial D_j is \int_{\partial D_j}d\phi and may be positive or negative. The old paper elsewhere correctly establishes flux as the normal integral \int_{\partial D_j}\partial_\nu\phi\,|dz|. The material difference is that the displayed d\phi integral is tangential and vanishes on a closed curve, while the normal integral can describe a nonzero source or sink.
issues.overall_effect: The physical interpretation in this introductory viewpoint is wrong, but the later theorems and their flux proofs already use the correct normal-derivative integral and remain valid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair:
Replace the displayed exact-differential identity by the normal-flux formula $A_j=\int_{\partial D_j}
abla\phi\cdot
u\,|dz|=\int_{\partial D_j}\partial_
u\phi\,|dz|$, or its equivalent oriented coordinate form, and base the source/sink interpretation on that quantity. No later formal result requires alteration.
issues.why_classification: The exact-differential formula is a genuine mathematical misidentification: its integral is zero, so the accompanying nonzero source/sink interpretation does not follow as written. The preceding discussion already supplies the correct normal-flux quantity, making the repair short, local, and routine while leaving all formal results unchanged.

issues.title: Wrong sign in the complex Green-function representation
issues.failure_explanation: Since (z-\overline z)^2=-4 Im(z)^2, the displayed plus sign gives Re f_G=-(2\pi)^{-1}\log|\vartheta_1(z)|-Im(z)^2/(2b), contradicting the defining formula for G. The proof's one-line calculation is therefore invalid.
issues.overall_effect: Item (3) of the complex-layer lemma is false. Its other two items, which are the ones used later, are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In item (3) of Lemma `lem: Complex layer`, replace $+(z-\overline z)^2/(8b)$ by $-(z-\overline z)^2/(8b)$ and amend the one-line calculation to use $z-\overline z=2i\operatorname{Im}z$, so that the real quadratic term is $+\operatorname{Im}(z)^2/(2b)$.
issues.why_classification: The proof explicitly relies on the false algebraic calculation, so this is more than a transcriptional sign typo. Nevertheless, the defining formula for $G$ uniquely forces a local sign correction and a one-line proof repair, preserving the lemma item exactly and requiring no downstream changes.

issues.title: Wrong Green points in the Dirichlet block matrix

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Here, $\beta_k$, $k \in [M]$, are arbitrarily fixed points in $D_k$.

issues.failure_explanation: In e:DirIntEqAdisc, the coefficient of A_k at every target node is G(z_i^l-\beta_k). Consequently, the last row of B must contain G(z^M_{N_M}-\beta_k). The printed s_k entries neither denote the prescribed points nor yield the claimed matrix representation.
issues.overall_effect: The detailed block matrix, if implemented literally, does not implement the preceding discrete Dirichlet system, although that preceding system and the continuous theorem remain correct.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the final row of the displayed block $B$, replace every $s_k$ by $\beta_k$, giving entries $G(z^M_{N_M}-\beta_1),\ldots,G(z^M_{N_M}-\beta_M)$.
issues.why_classification: The preceding discrete system and the other rows of $B$ uniquely force the fixed points $\beta_k$; the isolated $s_k$ symbols are copied-index notation with no role in the construction. Correcting them requires no mathematical inference or algorithmic redesign.

issues.title: Unweighted transpose claim for the adjoint discretization

failure_location.quote: Note that \( D_s = D^T \), where $D$ is defined in Appendix~\ref{s: dirichlet num implementation}.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims D_s=D^T. The old matrix definitions actually give D_{ij}=h_jK_{ij} and (D_s)_{ij}=h_jK_{ji}; hence, for H=diag(h_i), they establish D_s=H^{-1}D^TH. The distinction is material whenever the arc-length weights h_i are not all equal, although the separately displayed formula for D_s itself remains usable.
issues.overall_effect: Using the claimed transpose shortcut would misweight the adjoint operator on nonuniform or nonconstant-speed boundary discretizations, affecting the Neumann and Steklov matrices. The separately specified D_s matrix is not defeated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the claim $D_s=D^T$ by $D_s=H^{-1}D^TH$, where $H=\operatorname{diag}(h_i)$ after globally indexing the quadrature nodes. Neumann and Steklov implementations should either assemble the separately displayed $D_s$ directly or use this weighted-transpose identity.
issues.why_classification: Deriving the weighted identity from $D_{ij}=h_jK_{ij}$ requires a genuine but elementary adjoint-weight check, and the unweighted shortcut would change the discretized operator. The correction is local and routine, preserves the same operators and numerical method, and needs no new lemma or substantive weakening.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: The discretization of the adjoint double-layer potential $\K^*$ is performed similarly to $\K$, where the diagonal limit is determined by Lemma~\ref{lem: properties double layer}(3).

issues.title: Double application of the parameter quadrature weight
issues.failure_explanation: To integrate the singular kernel against \phi(t)|z^{k\prime}(t)|dt, the product quadrature must apply R_j^k(s_i) to \phi_j|z^{k\prime}(s_j)|. The printed coefficient h_j^kR_j^k(s_i)=w_j^k|z^{k\prime}(s_j)|R_j^k(s_i) applies w_j^k again and mis-scales the singular block.
issues.overall_effect: The printed S_1^k matrix is not the stated product-quadrature discretization of the logarithmically singular integral, so a literal implementation has the wrong singular-block scaling.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For every entry of $S_1^k$, replace $h_j^kR_j^k(s_i^k)$ by $|z^{k\prime}(s_j^k)|R_j^k(s_i^k)$, equivalently by $h_j^kR_j^k(s_i^k)/w_j^k$, while retaining the factor $-1/(4\pi)$. Use this corrected singular block when assembling $S$.
issues.why_classification: The source's product-quadrature formula directly determines the correction, but recognizing that $R_j^k$ already contains the parameter-quadrature weight requires mathematical checking and repairs a systematic scaling error rather than a copied symbol. It is a short local rescaling that restores the intended quadrature without changing the method or its guarantees.

issues.title: Wrong node in the second single-layer diagonal entry
issues.failure_explanation: At row and column two, the diagonal limit is s\to t=s_2^k and therefore depends on |z^{k\prime}(s_2^k)|. Reusing |z^{k\prime}(s_1^k)| changes the matrix for a nonconstant-speed parametrization and does not implement the preceding limit formula.
issues.overall_effect: The printed smooth-remainder matrix has an incorrect second diagonal entry, so a literal implementation can perturb the single-layer matrix on general parametrizations.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the $(2,2)$ entry of $S_2^k$, replace $|z^{k\prime}(s_1^k)|$ by $|z^{k\prime}(s_2^k)|$. Consistently, the $j$th diagonal entry uses $|z^{k\prime}(s_j^k)|$.
issues.why_classification: The preceding diagonal-limit formula and the row-column pattern uniquely force evaluation at the second node. This is an isolated copied index that can be corrected without repairing any inference or construction.

issues.title: Missing mean term in the discrete Steklov pencil
issues.failure_explanation: The old right-hand matrix represents \mathcal S(I-\mathcal M), not the stated modified operator \mathcal S_0=\mathcal S(I-\mathcal M)+\mathcal M. In particular, both sides of the printed pencil annihilate constant densities, whereas the correct right-hand operator maps a constant density to that constant and thereby represents the zero Steklov mode.
issues.overall_effect: The printed pencil is not a discretization of e: steklov bie and is singular on the constant-density subspace; it therefore does not, as written, represent the full Steklov problem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the printed pencil by $(D_s+\tfrac12 I)(I-M)\vec\phi=\sigma\,[S(I-M)+M]\vec\phi$ and use the same right-hand matrix in the generalized eigensolver. This includes the constant-density subspace and restores the zero Steklov mode.
issues.why_classification: Omitting $M$ genuinely changes the discrete operator and makes the printed pencil fail on constants, so it is not harmless notation. However, the definitions of $\mathcal S_0$ and the matrix $M$ already uniquely supply the missing term; adding it is a short, local repair that preserves the full Steklov formulation and requires no new analysis or proof architecture.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: For the modified single-layer potential $\S_0 = \S (I-\M) + \M$, we discretize the operators $\S$, $I$, and $\M$ as $N \times N$ matrices.
